chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding a man who bequeathed to his slave one-third of his wealth, he said: 'The slave is appraised, then it is seen what one-third of the deceased's estate amounts to. If the one-third is less than the value of the slave by the amount of a quarter of the value, the slave is freed for that quarter of his value. And if the one-third is more than the value of the slave, the slave is freed and what remains of the one-third after the value is paid to him.'
ai.seo_question: How is a slave's emancipation handled when bequeathed one-third of an estate?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of 'partial manumission' (tadbir) when a slave is bequeathed as a specific portion of the estate, ensuring the slave's freedom is secured even if the designated share is insufficient. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the estate bears the cost of fulfilling the bequest, prioritizing the slave's liberation over the heirs' retention of capital. This specific application of the one-third rule demonstrates the flexibility of wills in Shia fiqh to accommodate unique assets like slaves.
